audit.whatIsWrong: Level 3 was scored to Heimerdinger while its why called the stage 'a wash', and levels 6, first item and 2+ items were all scored Skill against the mirror's reading.
audit.why: This is a front-loaded scaling matchup, not an even one: Heimerdinger owns every stage up to and including 6, and Dr. Mundo takes both item stages and never gives them back. The mirror set exactly that as an atomic group.
audit.corrected: Level 6 to Heimerdinger, first item and 2+ items to Dr. Mundo, on both layers, with ratings moved to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 row was generic template text and the page carried no cooldown sequencing at all — the packet flags that defect explicitly.
audit.why: Maximum Dosage is a flat 120s that heals a percent of missing health; Heart Zapper is 17/16.5/16/15.5/15s; Infected Bonesaw is 4s at 975 range; CH-2 is a flat 11s. Those give the concrete 'bait then stun' sequencing the page lacked.
audit.corrected: Level 6 keyed to UPGRADE!!! landing the stun his passive can no longer eat; first item and late keyed to Sunfire/Heartsteel and the 120s R.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mundo's passive was called 'Adrenaline Rush' — a name that does not exist in his kit — and the single most important interaction in the matchup was missing entirely: his passive resists the first immobilizing effect that hits him.
audit.why: Goes Where He Pleases resists the first immobilize, costing him health and dropping a cannister he can pick up to heal and reduce the passive's cooldown. Against a champion whose only hard CC is one grenade, that means the first CH-2 direct hit does nothing — you must bait it out first. The grenade is also CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade, 11s flat, stunning only the direct hit, and the turret's secondary attack is a pass-through beam with no slow.
audit.corrected: Bait Goes Where He Pleases with a throwaway grenade, then land the real CH-2 direct hit; his cannister pickup refunds the passive's cooldown, so track that too.

audit.why: Anti-heal is already listed early, which is correct against Heart Zapper's stored-damage heal and Maximum Dosage's percent-missing-health heal.

edits.before: Mundo is one of the weakest early laners in the game and your turret nest punishes exactly that. Level 1 you have only one charged turret and no stun, so don't shove into his cleaver — bank charges and respect that he picks the dropped cleaver back up to refund mana-free poke. By Level 2-3 your second turret plus the slowing electron beam fence off his casting spot, and his Adrenaline Rush regen is still too thin to soak your turret damage and trade back, so you zone his last-hits and chip him out. Don't burn your CH-3X grenade chasing a kill here; use the center-stun to deny CS and anchor the zone.
edits.after: Mundo is one of the weakest early laners in the game and your turret nest punishes exactly that. Level 1 you have only one charged turret and no stun, so don't shove into his cleaver — bank charges and respect that he picks the dropped cannister back up to refund health. By Level 2-3 your second turret plus its pass-through beam fence off his casting spot, and his regen is still too thin to soak your turret damage and trade back, so you zone his last-hits and chip him out. Don't burn CH-2 chasing a kill here; his passive eats the first immobilize anyway.

edits.before: Your nest is fully online — three banked turrets, the slowing electron beams, and the CH-3X center-stun — and a melee Mundo who walks in eats all of it. The problem is his percent-HP Q cleaver plus his passive regen heal back faster than your beams chip, so you own the SPACE and his CS but you never get the kill. At 6 your UPGRADE!!! super-turret or wider-stun grenade extends the zone, but once he finishes his first tank item (Sunfire/Heartsteel) the math flips: he facetanks the buildings and walks you down through the beam and grenade slows. Trade your zone control into plates and roams now, not into a fight you cannot close.

At 6 your UPGRADE!!! super-turret or longer stun extends the zone, but once he finishes Sunfire or Heartsteel the math flips: he facetanks the buildings and walks you down through the slows. Trade your zone control into plates and roams now.

edits.before: This is where Mundo simply wins if the game goes long. Maximum Dosage (R) on top of stacked HP and resists makes him unkillable — three turrets and a center-stun stop out-DPSing a heal that big, and your squishy yordle has no answer once he is itemized to walk through the nest. Your favor was entirely front-loaded in the laning phase. Cash that early zone lead into objectives, vision and a sidelane siege before ~25 minutes, because past that he out-stats the turret economy and out-scales you forever.
edits.after: This is where Mundo simply wins if the game goes long. Maximum Dosage on a flat 120s, on top of stacked HP and resists, makes him unkillable — three turrets and a direct-hit stun stop out-DPSing a heal that big, and your squishy yordle has no answer once he is itemized to walk through the nest. Your favor was entirely front-loaded in the laning phase. Cash that early zone lead into objectives, vision and a sidelane siege before ~25 minutes, because past that he out-stats the turret economy and out-scales you forever.

notes: 'Adrenaline Rush' was a fabricated passive name appearing in whys[0], spikes[0] and early; the real passive is Goes Where He Pleases and its immobilize-resist is the decisive mechanic in this lane. Maximum Dosage is percent-health healing, so stacking raw resistances is not the counter — Grievous Wounds is.
